requirement: Federal agencies are required to consult with the National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS) on any action that may result in adverse effects to Essential Fish Habitat (EFH).
scope: Offshore wind energy development activities on the Outer Continental Shelf (OCS) of the Gulf of Mexico (GOM) authorized by the Bureau of Ocean Energy Management (BOEM), undertaken by Federal agencies.
source: Section 305(b)(2) of the Magnuson-Stevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act (MSA); final rule (67 FR 2376) implementing EFH provisions (January 17, 2002); 50 CFR §§ 600.805 to 600.930
related_domains: environmental impact assessment; fisheries protection; regulatory compliance

requirement: All potential impacts to hard bottom features from bottom-disturbing activities will be avoided or mitigated to no adverse effect.
scope: Call Area; hard bottom features; bottom-disturbing activities
source: BOEM review and conditioning of permitted activities; adherence to proposed mitigations, monitoring, and reporting standards listed in Section 6 Proposed Mitigation Guidance.
related_domains: environmental protection; habitat preservation; impact mitigation; monitoring; reporting

requirement: BOEM is not authorizing any activities in state waters and onshore areas.
scope: Activities in state waters and onshore areas related to wind energy leases.

requirement: BOEM does not have the regulatory authority to apply mitigation measures outside of the OCS.
scope: Areas outside the Outer Continental Shelf (OCS).

requirement: Lessees would be responsible for obtaining any permits or other clearances required for operations conducted in state waters.
scope: Operations conducted in state waters by wind energy lessees.

requirement: All bottom-disturbing activity avoid physical impacts to all hard bottom habitats.
scope: Bottom-disturbing activities (specifically geotechnical and benthic habitat surveys) within lease areas and export cable corridors, applicable to hard bottom habitats.
source: BOEM’s proposed mitigation, monitoring, and reporting standards in Section 6 Proposed Mitigation Guidance.
related_domains: environmental impact assessment; habitat protection; survey methodology

requirement: It is expected that physical impacts to all hard bottom features will be avoided.
scope: Activities that disturb the seafloor, specifically impacting hard bottom habitats (e.g., HAPCs) and their associated communities, including slow-growing corals, during HRG surveys.
related_domains: environmental protection; habitat preservation; seafloor disturbance; geophysical surveys

scope: Geotechnical and benthic habitat surveys in areas with hard bottom habitats, including inshore hard bottom habitats such as oyster beds.
related_domains: environmental protection; habitat preservation; geotechnical surveys; benthic surveys

requirement: lease stipulations would distance bottom disturbing survey activities from sensitive, benthic habitats (e.g., hard bottoms)
scope: bottom disturbing survey activities; sensitive, benthic habitats
related_domains: environmental protection; habitat preservation; site characterization; survey operations

requirement: Trash and debris disposal at sea is prohibited.
scope: At sea (applicable to vessels involved in offshore wind farm activities)
source: USCG (International Convention for the Prevention of Pollution from Ships [MARPOL], Annex V, Public Law 100-220 [101 Stat. 1458])
related_domains: environmental protection; waste management; vessel operations; water quality

requirement: Lessees, applicants, operators, or holders of a ROW grant, RUE grant, or Alternate Use RUE grant are required to take measures to prevent unauthorized discharge of pollutants including marine trash and debris into the offshore environment.
scope: Offshore environment; applicable to lessees, applicants, operators, or holders of a ROW grant, RUE grant, or Alternate Use RUE grant
related_domains: environmental protection; waste management; pollution control; offshore operations; regulatory compliance

requirement: Hard bottom habitats would be identified (via HRG surveys) and avoided during met buoy placement and during geotechnical and benthic habitat sampling.
scope: Call and Project Areas; during met buoy placement, geotechnical sampling, and benthic habitat sampling.
source: avoidance standards outlined above (see Section 6 Proposed Mitigation Guidance)
related_domains: environmental protection; habitat preservation; site surveying

scope: Artificial reefs within the context of Essential Fish Habitat (EFH) designations in the Gulf of Mexico
